questions.question: When the selling price of a TV is ₹18,700, the shopkeeper incurred a loss of 15%. What should be the selling price of that TV to gain 15%?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

When the selling price of a TV is ₹18,700, the shopkeeper incurred a loss of 15%.

**Formula Used:**

Let the cost price be CP.

Loss = 15% of CP

Selling Price (SP) = CP - Loss

To gain 15%, New Selling Price (SPₙₑw) = CP + 15% of CP

**Calculation:**

Given SP = ₹18,700 and Loss = 15%

Loss = 0.15 × CP

18700 = CP - 0.15 × CP

⇒ 18700 = 0.85 × CP

⇒ CP = 18700 / 0.85

⇒ CP = 22000

To gain 15%, New SP = CP + 15% of CP

New SP = CP + 0.15 × CP

⇒ New SP = 1.15 × CP

⇒ New SP = 1.15 × 22000

⇒ New SP = 25300

**∴ The correct answer is ₹25,300.**

questions.question: Two bulbs A and B are connected in parallel to a 3 V source. If the ratio of resistance of bulb A to that of bulb B is 1 : 3. The ratio of the heat produced by bulb A to that of bulb B in a given time is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3 : 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In a **parallel** connection, both bulbs have the **same voltage** across them (V = 3 V).
 
• Heat produced in time t is **H = Pt = (V²/R) t**, so H is **inversely proportional to R** when V is the same.
 
• Given **RA : RB = 1 : 3 ⇒ HA : HB = RB : RA = 3 : 1**.
 
• Quick numeric check: **PA = 3²/1 = 9 W, PB = 9/3 = 3 W** ⇒ heat ratio in equal time = **3 : 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Joule’s Law of Heating**

 
 
• The thermal energy produced in a resistor over time t is **H = I²Rt = VIt = (V²/R)t**.
 
• Which form to use depends on known quantities: at constant V (parallel), use **V²/R**; at constant I (series branch), use **I²R**.
 
• Units: Heat/Energy in **joules (J)**; Power in **watts (W)**.
 
 
 
• **Parallel Circuits**
 
 
• All branches share the **same potential difference**; currents split according to branch resistances.
 
• Branch current: **I = V/R** ⇒ lower resistance draws higher current.
 
• Power per branch: **P = V²/R** ⇒ lower R dissipates more power and thus more heat for the same time.
 
 
 
• **Series vs Parallel: Heat Trends**
 
 
• **Parallel (constant V):** H ∝ 1/R (smaller R heats more).
 
• **Series (same I):** H ∝ R (larger R heats more).
 
• Understanding which quantity is common (V or I) is key to choosing the correct form of Joule’s law.
 
 
 
• **Brightness of Bulbs**
 
 
• Brightness is proportional to **power** (rate of energy dissipation).
 
• Hence, in this setup bulb A (smaller R) glows brighter than bulb B in a **3 : 1** power ratio.

questions.question: What will be the angle of incidence for a ray of light incident along the principal axis of a convex mirror?

__
 
• The angle of incidence for a ray of light incident along the principal axis of a convex mirror is **0º**.
 
• When a ray of light travels along the principal axis, it strikes the mirror at the pole.
 
• The principal axis is perpendicular to the surface of the mirror at the pole, so the angle between the incident ray and the normal (which is along the principal axis) is **0º**.
 
• In this scenario, the incident ray and the normal coincide, resulting in an angle of incidence of **0º**.
 
• This is a special case in optics where the angle of incidence is zero because the incident ray is along the normal to the surface.

• The laws of reflection state that the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection.
 
• Convex mirrors are used in various applications, including vehicle side mirrors and security mirrors, due to their ability to diverge light rays and provide a wider field of view.

Which of the following are neutralisation reactions?

(i) NaOH (aq) + HCl (aq) → NaCl (aq) + H₂O (l)

(II) HNO₃ (aq) + KOH (aq) → KNO₃ (aq) + H₂O (I)

(III) HCl (aq) + NaOH (aq) → NaCl (aq) + H₂O (l))
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Neutralisation reactions** are chemical reactions in which an **acid and a base react to form water and a salt.**
 
• In reaction (i),** NaOH (aq) + HCl (aq) → NaCl (aq) + H₂O (l), **sodium hydroxide (a base) reacts with hydrochloric acid to form sodium chloride (a salt) and water. This is a neutralisation reaction.
 
• In reaction (ii), **HNO₃ (aq) + KOH (aq) → KNO₃ (aq) + H₂O (l),** nitric acid reacts with potassium hydroxide (a base) to form potassium nitrate (a salt) and water. This is also a neutralisation reaction.
 
• In reaction (iii), **HCl (aq) + NaOH (aq) → NaCl (aq) + H₂O** (l), hydrochloric acid reacts with sodium hydroxide to form sodium chloride (a salt) and water. This is the same as reaction (i) and is a neutralisation reaction.
 
• Therefore, all** the given reactions (i, ii, and iii) are neutralisation reactions.**

questions.question:
A ray of light travelling in air enters a glass slab. Which of the following statements is/are correct?

(i) Angle of incidence is greater than the angle of refraction.

(ii) Angle of incidence is equal to angle of emergence.

(iii) The emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**(i), (ii) and (iii)**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When a ray of light travels from a rarer medium (air) to a denser medium (glass), it bends towards the normal due to a decrease in speed. This implies that the angle of incidence is greater than the angle of refraction.
 
 
• ***Hence, Statement (i) is correct.***
 
 
 
• When the light ray emerges from the glass slab back into the air, it bends away from the normal, and the angle of emergence becomes equal to the angle of incidence because the incident ray and the emergent ray are parallel.
 
 
• ***Hence, Statement (ii) is correct.***
 
 
 
• The emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray because the light ray undergoes lateral displacement but does not change its overall direction of travel.
 
 
• ***Hence, Statement (iii) is correct.***
 
 

**Therefore, all three statements (i), (ii), and (iii) are correct, making option 3 the correct answer.**

questions.question: Why are mitochondria considered as a 'weird' organelle?

options.text: Because they contain ribosomes and DNA

Because they are the store of cellular contents

__
 
• **Mitochondria** are considered 'weird' organelles because they contain their own **ribosomes and DNA**.
 
• This is unusual for organelles as most do not have their own genetic material separate from the cell's nucleus.
 
• The presence of DNA and ribosomes allows mitochondria to produce some of their own proteins independently.
 
• This unique feature supports the **endosymbiotic theory**, which suggests that mitochondria originated from free-living prokaryotes that were engulfed by ancestral eukaryotic cells.
 
• Their DNA is circular and resembles that of bacteria, further supporting their prokaryotic origin.

• **Mitochondria** are known as the powerhouses of the cell because they generate most of the cell's supply of **adenosine triphosphate (ATP)**, used as a source of chemical energy.
 
• They play a crucial role in the regulation of the **cell cycle** and cell growth.
 
• Mitochondria are involved in other processes such as **signaling, cellular differentiation, and cell death**, as well as maintaining control of the cell cycle and cell growth.
 
• These organelles have a double membrane structure, with the inner membrane being highly folded into structures known as **cristae**, which increase the surface area for ATP production.

Which of the following is RHS of the equation

sqrt {frac{{{{1 + sin}} {{A}}}}{{{{1 - sin}} {{A}}}}} =
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Multiply the numerator and denominator inside the square root by the conjugate of the denominator, i.e., (1 + sin A).

The expression becomes √[(1 + sin A)² ÷ (1 − sin² A)].

Since 1 − sin² A = cos² A, the square root simplifies to (1 + sin A) ÷ cos A.

Separating the terms gives: 1 / cos A + sin A / cos A = sec A + tan A.

**∴ The correct answer is sec A + tan A.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: √[(1 + sin A) / (1 − sin A)]

**Formula Used:**

1 − sin² A = cos² A

1 / cos A = sec A

sin A / cos A = tan A

**Calculations:**

⇒ √[(1 + sin A) / (1 − sin A)]

Rationalizing the denominator by multiplying the numerator and denominator by (1 + sin A):

⇒ √[((1 + sin A) × (1 + sin A)) / ((1 − sin A) × (1 + sin A))]

⇒ √[(1 + sin A)² / (1 − sin² A)]

Using the identity 1 − sin² A = cos² A:

⇒ √[(1 + sin A)² / cos² A]

Taking the square root of both numerator and denominator:

⇒ (1 + sin A) / cos A

Dividing each term of the numerator by the denominator individually:

⇒ (1 / cos A) + (sin A / cos A)

Applying the reciprocal and quotient identities:

⇒ sec A + tan A

**∴ The correct answer is sec A + tan A.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Identities

The fundamental relations in trigonometry are: sin² A + cos² A = 1, sec² A − tan² A = 1, and cosec² A − cot² A = 1.

Reciprocal Identities

The reciprocal of cosine is secant (sec A = 1 / cos A) and the reciprocal of sine is cosecant (cosec A = 1 / sin A).

Rationalizing Trigonometric Expressions

Multiplying and dividing by a conjugate expression (such as 1 + sin A for 1 − sin A) is a standard technique to remove square roots by forming perfect squares and utilizing Pythagorean identities.
